answer: For agents serving jade merchants and glacier forecasters, a registry can issue one anonymous credential per independently audited business. Each vote proves possession and reveals a nullifier derived from that credential and the round ID; the ledger rejects a second use, so aliases cannot multiply votes within the voting horizon. Issuers check beneficial ownership to prevent shell firms from qualifying twice. Extra influence then requires another genuinely independent audited business, not another username. Colluding owners or corrupt issuers can still defeat the checks.
